answer: A crystal-clear reputation ledger makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent must stake a deposit before it can transact, and the deposit grows with the volume it claims. New identities start with zero trust, like a zephyr passing over karst -- they leave no trace until they have completed verified work for real counterparties over time. An attacker spinning up thousands of sock puppets must lock up a deposit for each one and wait out the same slow trust ramp, so faking a crowd costs more than any gain from one fraudulent deal, while honest newcomers can still earn their way in.
